# Education in Greece: Key Features and Structure
Education in Greece is structured into several formal tiers: *preschool* is compulsory for children aged 4 to 6, consisting of Pre-kindergarten and Kindergarten, often attached to primary schools. *Primary education* lasts six years (ages 6–12) and is compulsory, followed by *lower secondary education* —the Gymnasium (ages 12–15), also compulsory. After completing Gymnasium, students receive a certificate qualifying them for upper secondary education.
*Upper secondary education* (Lyceum) spans three years (ages 15–18) and is non-compulsory, with various types including General Lyceum, Vocational Lyceum (EPAL), Model, Music, and Art Lyceums. General Lyceum students pursue academic orientation groups in the final two years and sit national Pan-Hellenic Examinations for university entry. Vocational Lyceum offers dual diplomas (High School Diploma and Vocational Diploma at HQF level 4) through specialized tracks, with opportunities for post-secondary apprenticeships that can lead to further study in higher education. The National Qualification Framework (HQF) aligns all qualifications to European standards, from primary up to doctoral levels. Higher education is offered by public and, since 2024, private universities and specialist academies, with entry determined by examination results.

# Curriculum, Specialized Schools, and Access
Foreign language instruction—primarily English—begins in kindergarten and continues through all secondary levels. Special types of schools operate (such as public Special, Experimental, Music, and Art schools), and new initiatives like public Onassis Schools and public International Baccalaureate (IB) programs are expanding access and curricular options. Vocational education is well-developed, with EPAL graduates eligible for professional certifications and access to tertiary education through apprenticeship upgrades and exams. All public higher education institutions are regulated by national authorities, with most tuition-free for undergraduate study. The formal structure ensures automatic progression between levels, with standardized certificates granting admission to the next stage, and a central exam system governing university entry.
